Crumb: how are changes in a running Chrome session saved back to the
vault?
New engineers · A running state-mode supervisor: autosave timer, crumb sync/close signals, snapshot, merge, encrypted write.

Detached process
that autosaves the
session

Key: frames = trust/deployment zones; box = runtime actor/process; cylinder = stored state. Arrows: caller → recipient,
response included; dashed = async; solid = sync; dotted = local command/I/O. Flow type is also written on each arrow.

setInterval every --autosave s (default
30; 0 disables), SIGUSR2 (crumb
sync), final save on SIGINT/SIGTERM.
Closing Chrome directly exits with no
final save.

Unchanged snapshots are skipped;
overlapping saves share one in-flight
save. Changes are 3-way merged
onto the vault's latest copy, written
via temp+rename. Errors are only
logged.

crumb sync polls the handle up to 10s
for a new lastSavedAt and returns
without error if nothing changed.
crumb close waits 30s, then SIGKILLs,
which skips the final save.
Outside this view: Launch, inject and handle startup handshake (launchDetached); Profile mode, login, capture and check flows.
